Spaghetti and straw triangle build: given 3 parts, can you make two different ones?

Goal: I can test which sets of three parts build only one triangle.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Triangles have six parts: three sides and three angles. How many must match to guarantee a congruent copy? Try building triangles from three given parts.

With SSS (three sides), SAS (two sides and the angle between them) or ASA (two angles and the side between them), every triangle you build is congruent to every other. With SSA (two sides and an angle not between them) you can sometimes build two different triangles. With AAA, triangles can have the same shape but different sizes.

slides.html:
Fix three parts (SSS, SAS, SSA, AAA) and drag to find a second triangle.

Use the controls in the panel. Drag the hollow points on the board.
